strengths: One engine for the floor: floor-machine.mjs `nextFloor` is pure and every writer hands its answer to one write, trial-floor.mjs `commitFloor` (floor-machine.mjs:497-699, trial-floor.mjs:628-674); the bar's greyed buttons ask the same rows (trial-floor.mjs:1431-1442).
One writer in one queue: the floor is written only on the primary GM inside a step of `SEIZE_KEY`, another GM asks `trial.gm`, and no step calls a public writer (trial-floor.mjs:350-371, 726-742).
The Objection is judged, paid, posted and opened on the primary, its target read off the primary's own voice Room, and the price is handed back when the floor did not move (trial.mjs:1070-1171).

A card is built from `HOLDER_FIELDS` of the bullet as the GMs hold it, never from the GM half of `truthBulletData` (trial.mjs:530-536, 1205-1222); truth-bullets.mjs keeps the two halves in separate fields.
A player's own card carrying the trial's flags is raised on no screen and is marked refused by the primary (trial.mjs:631-656).

A late press cannot move a newer floor: the GM's Now names the floor it saw (trial-floor.mjs:1613-1643), a round's Done, Pass and step over name the step they are for (floor-machine.mjs:609-616), and a step over is heard once a sender and step (trial-modes.mjs:166-171).

Who volunteered for the Closing and whom the draw named stay in the GMs' store; the floor holds a count, and `via` is 'chosen' whether the GM confirmed or changed the draw (trial-modes.mjs:226-251, floor-machine.mjs:186-189; world-secrets.mjs:123-128 holds the setting to it).
The trial record's fields are one table with a lifetime and a writer each (trial-progress.mjs:339-384), and another GM's patch is held to `RECORD_FIELDS` on the primary (trial-progress.mjs:514-522).
Every countdown is counted from one stamp on the server's clock, and the picker, the primary's test and the lapse read one millisecond count (trial-floor.mjs:765-768, 1182-1186, 1685-1692).
The sentence is carried out on the primary under one latch, a record written after each student and the stamp only when nobody failed (trial-progress.mjs:94-110, 153-201).
What cannot be undone is the destructive role and never the default in every window of the console (trial-floor-ui.mjs:584-625, 1503-1518, 1849-1886).
The speakers' record lives in memory only, is emptied at both edges of the trial, and names only a student alive as the table knows it (trial-speakers.mjs:101-107, 214-221).
`MODE_RULES` states who speaks, presents, objects and may be aimed at for every mode in one table, and `MODE_STARTS` is held to the modes by a census (trial-floor.mjs:98-151).

findings.title: Keep speaking, the default of Your turn, takes Done and Pass away for the rest of the turn: nothing else on the speaker's screen can end it
findings.where: scripts/trial-prompt.mjs:175-176 (the turn marked as prompted before the window opens), 189-198 (the window, Keep speaking the primary), 214 (the only reset, after a thesis), 217-220; scripts/bridge-asks.mjs:405 (requestTurn, called by trial-prompt.mjs alone); lang/en.json:3541, 3544
findings.what_happens: `promptTurn` sets `promptedFor = key` for the turn's step and opens Your turn with Keep speaking as the primary (so Enter and Space press it), Done and Pass on the left. Any answer but Done or Pass - Keep speaking, Escape, the header's X - returns with `promptedFor` still the key, and the once-a-second `tick` then finds `promptedFor === key` and opens nothing. Only the Scrum thesis branch clears it. `requestTurn` with `done` or `pass` has no other caller in scripts/ (git grep: trial-prompt.mjs:220 only), and the HUD and the voice tile carry no turn control. So after the default answer the speaker cannot end or pass the turn; it runs to its clock (30-120 s in Testimony, up to 300 s in the Closing Argument) unless a GM presses Skip.
findings.failure_scenario: The Closing's speaker clears the window with Enter (Keep speaking) to see their sheet, finishes after two minutes and finds no Done: the table sits through the remaining three minutes, or the player has to ask the GM to press Skip or End this mode.
findings.expected: The window's own words, 'Press Done when you finish, or Pass to give up your turn.' (lang/en.json:3541), and the handbooks: 'a window says Your turn (n s), with Done to end your turn and Pass to give it to the next speaker' (player-handbook.en.md:894; gm-handbook.en.md:1553). Keep speaking as the default is the owner's card (E70 fix p2-G3; docs/design/windows.md M13); that it removes the two controls is written nowhere.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep a way back for the running step: clear `promptedFor` when the window closes without Done or Pass and reopen it from a control on the trial row or the voice tile, or leave a small Done / Pass control there for the speaker.
findings.refutation_tried: git grep of requestTurn, ACTION_TRIAL_TURN and DRPG.Trial.turn over scripts/: the window is the only asker of done and pass. hud.mjs `objectionControl` (1511-1580) is the trial row's one control. The comment at trial-prompt.mjs:194-197 says the default 'closes the window alone; the turn runs on its clock, the GM's bar still skips it' - it records the default, not that Done should be gone. A reload reopens the window (the latch is the browser's memory), which is no road a player is told.
findings.tests_near: R1365 (tier 1) pins the footer's order and roles; R1047's part 4 (tests-tier1.mjs:33230) pins that Done and Pass are not the default; tier 2 E70-T9 drives a round with the heartbeat held. None closes the window with Keep speaking and then looks for Done.

findings.title: A trial console opened from the GM panel hands the panel back the first time it reopens itself: the reopen runs outside the awaited chain
findings.where: scripts/trial-floor-ui.mjs:1675-1702 (the live hook's close and detached reopen), 1805, 1826-1829 (the awaited chain); scripts/gm-panel.mjs:266-267, 451-452 (the console's two doors), 599-618 (the tile runner that reopens the panel)
findings.what_happens: The GM panel closes itself, awaits the tile's `run()` and opens again when it resolves with anything but RAISED. `manageClassTrial` keeps that promise alive across footer actions by returning the next console (`return manageClassTrial()`). But when the floor's family or the trial's running state changes while the console stands open, the live hook closes the dialog and reopens the console from a detached `.then`. The close resolves the awaited window with null, the tile's `run()` resolves, and `openGmPanel()` runs beside the new console. Changes that take this road: a rebuttal running out or skipped (debate to no floor), a mode started from the console's own picker (Nonstop Debate, Testimony, Panic Round, the Closing, the zone modes: the picker's click does not close the console), a round or the Closing ending by itself, the bar's End this mode, and a trial started or ended by another GM or from Edit campaign. The panel and the console are the only doors: git grep finds `manageClassTrial` in gm-panel.mjs and api.mjs alone.
findings.failure_scenario: The GM opens Class Trial from the panel, starts the trial and a debate; a player objects, the rebuttal runs out, and at that moment the GM panel opens over or beside the reopened console.
findings.expected: gm-panel.mjs:590-593: the panel comes back 'by the time `run()` resolves the screen is clear again'; here the screen holds the console the GM is running the trial from. One window for one question.
findings.fix_sketch: Let the first call's promise follow the reopened console (resolve the awaited chain with the reopened console's promise, or answer RAISED when the close was the console's own reopen).
findings.refutation_tried: Read the whole chain: `drpgWindow` resolves null on a close (`rejectClose: false`), line 1805 returns null for it, and gm-panel.mjs:615-617 reopens for any answer but RAISED. `openGmPanel` refuses only a panel already open (533-539), and the tile closed it first (605). After the first detached reopen the later ones belong to no chain, so the panel comes back once per console opened from it. Which of the two windows ends on top is not established (two unordered promises).
findings.tests_near: tier 0 R1026 holds the console's signature to the floor's family, and tier 2 E70-T2 (cited at trial-floor-ui.mjs:1377-1380) reads the console across an Objection; no test found opens it from the GM panel's tile. The same mechanism is reported for the incident tracker by the reader of murder-ui.mjs (domain-case-a-incident-3).
findings.live_check: Open Class Trial from the GM panel, start a trial and a debate, let an Objection and its rebuttal run out: count the windows.

findings.title: An Objection inside a Testimony is read as the debate's exchange: the console closes and reopens at its start and its end, its footer's step is Close Debate, and that press drops the rest of the round under a card saying the debate is closed
findings.where: scripts/trial-floor.mjs:100-101 (the Objection's and the rebuttal's family 'debate'), 154-158 (floorFamily: only the Closing's exchange is kept), 179-183 (TRIAL_NEXT_STEPS), 400 (the op `end`); scripts/trial-floor-ui.mjs:1385 (trialSignature), 1395-1406 (the footer's button), 498-509 (closeDebate); scripts/floor-machine.mjs:693-694 (End this mode in a round's exchange)
findings.what_happens: A Testimony allows an Objection at its speaker (`MODE_RULES.testimony.object`). The machine then writes mode `objection` and keeps `round` on the floor. `floorFamily` answers the Closing's exchange as 'closing' but a round's exchange by the mode's row, 'debate'. So (1) `trialSignature` moves from `true|round` to `true|debate` and back when the queue resumes, and the console closes and opens again each time - what E70-06 took out for a debate's Objection; (2) `trialNextStep` answers `closeDebate`, so the console's footer shows Close Debate in the primary's slot, and the GM panel's Next line and the vote window's lead read 'The debate is open. Close it when the room has argued it out.'; (3) Close Debate runs `closeDebate()` -> `endFloor()` -> the op `end`, which writes the empty floor: the round is gone with no 'The Testimony is over.' card, and the table is told 'The debate is closed'. The bar's End this mode in the same state resumes the queue at the next speaker (floor-machine.mjs:694), so the two ends of one state do different things.
findings.failure_scenario: Third speaker of a six-speaker Testimony is objected to; the GM's console flashes shut and open, now offers Close Debate, and the GM who presses it to end the argument loses the last three turns while every screen reads 'The debate is closed'.
findings.expected: gm-handbook.en.md:1553: in Testimony the Objection 'runs the debate's exchange ...; after it the round goes on at the next speaker', and 'End this mode (End the round) ends the round'; trial-floor.mjs:155 gives the Closing's exchange the Closing's footer for the same reason, and trial-floor-ui.mjs:1377-1384 says the console is not to reopen at an Objection.
findings.fix_sketch: Answer 'round' from `floorFamily` while `floor.round` holds a round (as `closingOf` does for the Closing), so the footer keeps End the round and the signature does not move.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that the round stays on the Objection's floor (floor-machine.mjs:564-567 spreads the floor; `roundOf` reads it at 65-68) and that no Closing field stands on a round's floor (the round's base at 528 has none, and every end writes `{}`). `closeDebate` asks nothing of the mode (trial-floor-ui.mjs:498-509) and the op `end` takes the Closing's road only (trial-floor.mjs:400). Enter is held in the exchange (1780-1784), so the press is a click. git grep of floorFamily in the tests: six lines (tests-tier0.mjs:17735-17764 and 23065, tests-tier1.mjs:52663), all on trialSignature's source text; none hands it a round's exchange.
findings.tests_near: R1026 (tier 0) holds trialSignature to floorFamily; R1042 (tier 1) reads the machine's round rows, an exchange inside one among them, without the console; R1048 reads the console for the Closing and the Reveal. No test draws the console on an Objection inside a round.

findings.title: The Closing Argument's refusals are written in both languages and never shown: Confirm on a drawn speaker whose player has dropped says only 'The Closing Argument did not change.'
findings.where: scripts/trial-modes.mjs:265-275 (closingCall); scripts/trial-floor.mjs:412-416 (the ops call closingStepInStep without `why`), 587-599; scripts/floor-machine.mjs:267-294 (the keys); lang/en.json:1761-1769 (the eight sentences), 1777 (notDone)
findings.what_happens: The machine refuses a Closing step with a key of its own: `absent` ('That player is not connected: pick someone else.'), `noDrawn`, `noChoice`, `notParticipant`, `noDecision`, `notInExchange`, `voteOpen`, `nothingToResume`. The GM's four calls - Confirm the speaker, Pick, the decision, Resume - go through `closingCall` -> `floorStep` -> `FLOOR_OPS`, which call `closingStepInStep(event)` without `{ why: true }`; a refusal becomes null, and `closingCall` says the one line `DRPG.Floor.closing.notDone`. git grep finds each of those eight keys in floor-machine.mjs and the tests only, so none is ever localized for a GM. On a GM who is not the primary the bridge first says its own 'nothing was carried out' (bridge-runs-records.mjs:829) and `closingCall` then adds the second notice.
findings.failure_scenario: The drawn volunteer's browser reloads during the GM's choice; the GM presses Confirm the speaker and reads 'The Closing Argument did not change.' with the row still offering Confirm, and has to guess that Pick someone else is the way on.
findings.expected: trial-floor.mjs:1400-1401 states the rule for the bar ('so a dead button says why'), and the eight sentences exist in en.json and pl.json for exactly these presses; trial-modes.mjs:95-96 made the same repair for a round's start (E70 fix p2-G3).
findings.fix_sketch: Have the Closing's ops ask `closingStepInStep(event, { why: true })` and carry the key back (or ask `nextFloor` on the pressing GM first, as `barMay` does) so `closingCall` localizes the machine's reason.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a pre-check on the pressing GM: `startClosing` has one (`closingRefusal`: already, busy); Confirm, Pick, the decision and Resume have none (trial-modes.mjs:294-314). `closingStepInStep(event, { why: true })` has one caller, `volunteerOnPrimary`, which maps every refusal to its own bridge text. The pick window lists connected participants only, so `absent` there needs a drop after it opened; the drawn speaker's and an objector's drop are the ordinary cases.
findings.tests_near: R1043 (tier 1) reads the machine's keys; R1048 reads the console's row. Neither presses a refused Confirm through `closingCall`.

findings.title: An Overrule after the exchange of an Objection raised in a Testimony or in the Closing Argument offers 'Open the debate again' with the interrupted speaker's seconds, as the trial's next step
findings.where: scripts/trial-floor.mjs:1540 (the offer written), 198 (the next step); scripts/trial.mjs:944-945 (the receipt: `mode`, `leftAtObjection`, `debateLeft`); scripts/floor-machine.mjs:380-383 (restOf); scripts/trial-floor-ui.mjs:1407-1412, 1535-1540
findings.what_happens: A receipt keeps what the Objection interrupted (`mode`), that floor's seconds (`leftAtObjection`) and `debateLeft`, the rest of the newest debate on the stack - null when the Objection cut into a round's turn or the Closing's speech, which have no debate under them. `overruleInStep`, for an Overrule after the exchange with no floor open, writes `againAfterOverrule.seconds` from `debateLeft ?? leftAtObjection` without asking the receipt's `mode`. So once the round or the Closing is over, overruling its newest Objection sets the offer with the speaker's seconds; `TRIAL_NEXT_STEPS` then answers `openAgain` (ahead of `reopen` and `openDebate`), the console's primary reads 'Open the debate again (n s left)' with the lead 'Open the debate again with the time it had left', and the press opens a debate of that length under the trial record's last question.
findings.evidence:
if (!judged.during && !floor) change.againAfterOverrule = { messageId: id, seconds: Number(judged.receipt?.debateLeft ?? judged.receipt?.leftAtObjection) || 0 };
...
                    mode: entry?.before?.mode ?? null, leftAtObjection: entry ? Number(entry.leftAtObjection) || 0 : null,
                    debateLeft: restOf(floor), trialStartedAt: record.trialStartedAt ?? null, at: serverNow(), overruled: false,
findings.failure_scenario: The Closing's speaker was objected to with 200 s left; the Closing ends, the GM overrules that Objection from the bar, and the console's next step becomes 'Open the debate again (200 s left)' where the ballots were next - a debate that never ran.
findings.expected: gm-handbook.en.md:1478: after its exchange 'the console offers Open the debate again with the time the debate had left'; trial-floor.mjs:1538-1539: 'The debate's time when the Objection cut in (the newest debate under it, TR31's rest)'. With no debate under the Objection there is nothing to offer.
findings.fix_sketch: Write the offer only when the receipt's `debateLeft` is a number (or its `mode` is the debate).
findings.refutation_tried: Read `keepReceipt` and `restOf`: a round's turn empties the stack (`before: []`, floor-machine.mjs:86) and the Closing's speech too (173), so the Objection's entry is the only one and its `before.mode` is the round's or 'closing'. `overruleTarget` names the newest receipt of this trial whatever its mode (floor-machine.mjs:476-487). `startFloorInStep` clears the offer only when a debate opens (trial-floor.mjs:902-905). grep of againAfterOverrule in the tests: views handed to `trialNextStep` and the record's blank; `debateLeft` once in tier 1.
findings.tests_near: R1027 and R1030 (tier 1) read the Overrule and the debate again for a debate's Objection; none writes the offer from a receipt whose `mode` is a round or the Closing.

findings.title: The Closing Argument's two waits for the GM (who speaks, who continues) raise nothing on the GM's side, and the GM panel's Next line reads 'End it, then send the ballots.' meanwhile
findings.where: scripts/floor-machine.mjs:311, 325 (the choice, `cards: []`), 210-220 (the decision); scripts/trial-floor.mjs:180 (the step `endClosing` for the whole Closing), 550-562 (the table's line); scripts/sfx.mjs:292-299; lang/en.json:1566, 1773, 1776
findings.what_happens: When the volunteers' 30 s end, and again when an exchange inside the Closing ends, the floor enters a phase with no clock that only a GM's press leaves. The players read 'The GM is confirming the speaker.' or 'The GM decides who continues the Closing Argument.' on the HUD and the Event panel. On the GM's side the machine posts no card for either move, sfx.mjs plays `closingStart` and a speaker's turn only, and nothing is whispered. The question is drawn in the console's row alone (`closingConsole`). With the console closed, the panel's Next line is the step `endClosing`: 'The Closing Argument holds the floor. End it, then send the ballots.'
findings.failure_scenario: An Objection's rebuttal ends three minutes into the Closing while the GM is reading the map with the console closed: the table waits on 'The GM decides who continues' and the GM's panel says to end the Closing.
findings.expected: The console's own lead says what is asked ('confirm or pick its speaker, and after an Objection decide who continues', lang/en.json:1632); the same question deserves a sign where the GM is when the console is shut - a notice, a sound or the Next line's words.
findings.fix_sketch: Give the choice and the decision a step of their own in `TRIAL_NEXT_STEPS` (or a notice to the GMs when the floor enters them).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a card, a whisper or a sound at the two moves: `closingFloor` returns the caller's `cards` (empty on the clock's road), `commitFloor` posts only those, sfx.mjs keys on the volunteers' stamp and a speaker's step. `drpgTrialStep` is called and has no listener (see hygiene). A GM who started the Closing half a minute ago is likely at the console for the first wait; the second comes minutes later.
findings.tests_near: R1043, R1048 (tier 1) read the phases and the console's row; none asks what a GM is told.

findings.title: While any mode but the debate holds the floor, Enter on a focused button of the console is swallowed, the bar's own buttons included
findings.where: scripts/trial-floor-ui.mjs:1780-1784 (the capture listener), 881-883 (exchangeRuns: every floor that is not a debate)
findings.what_happens: The listener meant to keep Enter from pressing the footer's default runs in the capture phase on the window's root and cancels every Enter keydown while `exchangeRuns()` - an Objection, a rebuttal, a round, the Closing, a zone mode. A button's activation by Enter is the default action of that keydown, so on a browser it never becomes a click: a GM who tabs to Skip, +30 s, Overrule or Confirm the speaker and presses Enter moves nothing and is told nothing. Space still presses.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM working by keyboard tabs to Skip during a rebuttal and presses Enter: nothing happens, though the lead reads 'Skip on the bar moves it on now'.
findings.expected: trial-floor-ui.mjs:846-849: a bar button stays 'still focusable', and a press 'says that reason'; the hold was written for the footer's default (1777-1779).
findings.fix_sketch: Cancel the key only when its target is not a button inside the bar, or hold the default by the footer's `default` alone (already Close in an exchange, 1516).
findings.refutation_tried: The listener has no test of the target (read at 1780-1784). The harness cannot show it: jsdom does not turn Enter on a button into a click, so tier 2's 'the console holds Enter while an Objection runs' (tests-tier2.mjs:48044) reads the same either way. That a real browser cancels the click with the keydown is browser behaviour, not read here.
findings.tests_near: Tier 2 'the console holds Enter while an Objection runs, ...' (tests-tier2.mjs:48044) measures the footer's default; no test presses Enter on a bar button.
findings.live_check: On a real browser, during a rebuttal, focus the bar's Skip with Tab and press Enter, then Space: the floor should move on both.

findings.title: Your turn's title states the whole turn when the speaker is given back only the rest of it
findings.what_happens: After an Objection in a Testimony lapses, is withdrawn or is overruled, `speakerAgain` gives the speaker the turn back with `seconds` the turn's full length and `startedAt` moved so that only the rest is left, and a new step. The speaker's window opens again for that step and takes its title from `floor.seconds`: 'Your turn (60 s)' with 23 s on the clock. The Closing's branch of the same line reads `secondsLeft`.
findings.failure_scenario: A Testimony speaker objected to at 23 s gets the floor back after the GM's Overrule and reads 'Your turn (60 s)'; the turn passes 23 s later.
findings.expected: The title names the seconds the speaker has (lang/en.json DRPG.Trial.turn.title, 'Your turn ({seconds} s)'); gm-handbook.en.md:1553: Overrule 'gives the speaker back the rest of their turn'.
findings.fix_sketch: Read `secondsLeft(floor)` for a round's turn as for the Closing's (rounded up for a Scrum turn's fraction).
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that the step moves (floor-machine.mjs:108) so the window does open again, and that nothing else rewrites the title (the window is static after it opens).
findings.tests_near: R1042 (tier 1) reads the machine's round rows, a turn given back with its rest among its fixtures (tests-tier1.mjs:32821); R1365 the footer. None reads the title.

findings.title: The mode picker greys Nonstop Debate with 'The debate is already running.' while a round, the Closing or a zone mode holds the floor
findings.what_happens: `modePickerHtml` gives every other start the reason `DRPG.Floor.round.busy` when a mode other than the debate holds the floor, but the debate's own start answers `DRPG.Floor.bar.inDebate` for any floor at all. The greyed button's title, and the notice a press on it shows (line 1753), therefore say a debate runs during a Testimony.
findings.failure_scenario: During a Panic Round the GM presses the greyed Nonstop Debate and reads 'The debate is already running.'
findings.expected: The machine's own reason for that start, `DRPG.Floor.startBusy`: 'A debate cannot open while a round, the Closing Argument, or a zone mode holds the floor. End that mode first.' (floor-machine.mjs:505; lang/en.json:1707).
findings.fix_sketch: Answer `startBusy` (or `busy`) when the floor's mode is not the debate, `inDebate` only for a debate.
findings.refutation_tried: `startFloor` itself says the machine's reason (trial-floor.mjs:884-888), but the picker never reaches it: a greyed button only shows its title.
findings.tests_near: tests-tier1.mjs:9327-9331 draws the picker with no floor; grep of `bar.inDebate` in the tests finds the bar's Back to the debate only (32324, 32370-32371). No test draws the picker in a round.

by_decision.what: An Objection whose Truth Bullet does not come - its seconds out, its picker closed, its floor replaced - is withdrawn with the price kept, and the floor goes back to the debate with the time the debate had.
Keep speaking is the default of Your turn and Someone else of the volunteers' window, so Enter ends and volunteers nothing.
After an Objection's exchange in a Testimony the round goes on at the next speaker; the interrupted speaker's rest is not given back, except by an Overrule.

by_decision.what: A rebuttal's end closes the floor (the trial's discussion), not a debate; the console then offers the debate again with the same question and budget.
An Objection may be aimed at a student whose death the GMs keep unpublished: the target is alive as the table knows it.
The trial's list of the dead, a death nobody has found among them, is world data while the Class Trial runs.
The console's footer step is Close Debate for the whole debate, an Objection and its rebuttal included, and Enter presses nothing while one runs.
The verdict and the End of chapter stand in the console's footer only while each is the trial's next step.
A debate is never shorter than 30 s, so the debate again after an Overrule with 12 s left opens with 30.
A Present is free, posted by the primary, and hands every other participant a copy as shown; with or without the Analyze result is the presenter's choice.

not_established: Whether a withdrawn or lapsed Objection that cut into a Rebuttal is meant to end that Rebuttal: the machine sends the floor to the debate with the debate's rest (floor-machine.mjs:437, 596) - in a round to the interrupted speaker (speakerAgain) - while an Overrule of the same Objection gives the pair their Rebuttal back with its time (672-685). gm-handbook.en.md:1464 states the rule for a debate only; no test hands `lapse` or `withdraw` a stack of two. The owner's word would settle it: as written, one press of OBJECTION! and a closed picker ends two other players' Rebuttal for the price of an Objection.
Whether Enter on a focused bar button is in fact cancelled on Foundry's browsers (finding 7): the listener is read, the browser's default action is not measurable in jsdom.

How often a sentence is left never attempted (the comment against trial-progress.mjs:113-118): it needs a reload of the primary between the phase write and the first kill on the Edit campaign road, or a primary that stays connected and answers `execute` neither from `closeTrial` nor from `reconcilePhase`. The condition is read; the timing was not measured.
Which window ends on top when the console reopens itself and the GM panel returns (finding 2): the two opens are unordered promises; a table would show it.

Whether what an objector paid is meant to be readable by every browser: the receipt in the world's trial record holds `paid: { key, pay, amount, grant }` by card (trial.mjs:943). world-secrets.mjs has no rule for it and 72-canary's scan was not run here.

Whether a Monocub holding a Truth Bullet is meant to Present: `presentOnPrimary` judges the death, the mode's row and the bullet (trial.mjs:377-394) and does not ask `isMonocub`, while the copies go to `trialParticipants`, which leaves a Monocub out. No comment or handbook line read here says either way.

Whether the console's tick (one rebuild of the whole region a second while a floor is open, twice the reading of the trial with `after`) costs anything a table feels: the code says it is deliberate (trial-floor-ui.mjs:1705-1724); `perf()`'s `live..drpg-trial-console` line at a table is the reading.
